summary: - g) Aggrieved by the Impugned Order passed by the State Commission, the Appellant has preferred the present appeal. - **b. Whether the appellant is empowered to impose Liquidated Damages in terms of Clause 4.6 of the PPA dated 28.03.2013?** - **f. Whether there is no other provision in the PPA under which the Appellant can levy liquidated damages and recover the same as held by the Ld. Commission?** 7. We have heard at length the learned counsel for the parties and considered carefully their written submissions, arguments putforth during the hearings etc. Gist of the same is discussed hereunder. 8. The learned counsel for the Appellant has made following arguments/submissions for our consideration on the issues raised by it: - i) The State Commission also erred in holding that the decision of Board of Directors of the Appellant is assailed as the Respondent No. 2 has only challenged the communication dated 2.12.2015. to be shifted and the delay in commissioning of the Solar Project is beyond its control. However, the Appellant vide letter dated 2.12.2015 granted extension of SCOD till 31.3.2016 along with levy of penalty of Rs. 9.52 Cr. which was to be deposited by 15.12.2015. The Respondent No. 2 vide letter dated 11.12.2015 requested the Appellant to reconsider its decision of imposing the penalty. The Appellant vide letter dated 17.12.2015 re-iterated its stand in letter dated 2.12.2015. The Respondent No. 2 filed petition with the State Commission on 18.1.2016. On 21.1.2016 the State Commission stayed the encashment of the PBG of the Respondent No. 2 by the Appellant. On 16.3.2016 vide the Impugned Order the State Commission has rightly set aside the letter dated 2.12.2015 of the Appellant by holding that the delay was due to reason attributable to the Discom (JdVVNL) and fall under Clause 4.5.1 (a) of the PPA and accordingly the the application of Clause 4.6 of the PPA gets excluded. Further there is no other provision in the PPA under which LD can be imposed. The action of the Appellant is also contrary to the Section 74 of the Contracts Act 1872. 11. **After having a careful examination of all the aspects brought before us on the issues raised in Appeal and submissions made by the Appellant and the Respondents for our consideration, our observations are as follows:-** - a. The present case pertains to decision of the State Commission vide its Impugned Order setting aside the letter date 2.12.2015 of the Appellant regarding levy of LD on Respondent No. 2 while granting extension of SCOD till 31.3.2016. ii. Now let us see the analysis of the State Commission as given in the Impugned Order and the relevant extract is reproduced below: _line. Despite the request of Petitioner and Respondent, the line was not removed by Discom. Therefore, Respondent cannot find fault with the Petitioner for not fulfilling the obligation undertaken by it under Article 4.1 of PPA for commissioning the plant as per SCOD and impose liquidated damages on the Petitioner on this account.”_ _provision in the PPA under which Respondent may levy liquidated damages and recover the same.””_ iii. In view of the above, the issues raised in Question Nos. 6. a. and 6. g. are decided against the Appellant. _“25.Further, the learned Counsel appearing for Respondent, during the course of arguments, defended the action taken by the Respondent also by producing some additional documents. Of these, two of the additional documents produced are related to the agenda placed before the BoD and the decision taken by the Board on it._ _26. Relying on these two documents, the Ld. Counsel contended that the_ _ Petitioner committed default in completing the project due to non achievement of -_ _ financial closure and the plea that non shifting of transmission line was not the real reason and therefore, action taken is in accordance with the PPA. _ _27.While appreciating the efforts of the Respondent in defending its action,_ _ we are unable to accept the defense put forward. On the first count, the reason now being cited on behalf of Respondent for levying penalty is not the reason which is communicated to the Petitioner on dt. 2.12.2015. The second is that the said -_ _ ground of non achievement of financial closure was not sustainable on the day on which decision was taken by the Board of RREC. As pointed out by the Petitioner’s Counsel, the Petitioner vide its letter dt. 21.08.2015 (para 2) had already informed the Respondent that they have achieved the financial closure with PTC Financial Services Ltd. and loan disbursement is expected to be done in one or two weeks in September, 2015. Once financial closure was stated to_ _ have been achieved by the Petitioner before action is taken, the said ground was no longer available to the Respondent to state that the condition of PPA is violated.” _ The State Commission in its Impugned Order concluded that the reason for imposition of LD was not mentioned in the letter dated 2.12.2015 of the Appellant to the Respondent No. 2 and the ground of non-achievement of financial closure was not sustainable on the day on which decision was taken by the Board of the Appellant. Further, the Respondent No. 2 had already got sanction of loan from IREDA in March’ 2015 and from SBBJ in August’ 2015. The issue of shifting of the Electric Poles was also going on between the parties at that point of time. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case as detailed out above, we are in agreement with findings of the State Commission. _“13.We observe that this case is similar to M/s Arjun Green Power Pvt. Ltd. (petition no. 586/15) and a similar relief was claimed. Counsels appearing for the parties also submitted that the case is similar to M/s Arjun Green Power Pvt. Ltd. Commission after considering the facts in the petition of M/s_ The Impugned Order dated 16.3.2016 passed by the State Commission is hereby upheld.
title: Rajasthan Renewable Energy CorporationLtd. (RRECL) Versus Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission (RERC).
